title: Efficiency and effectiveness
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-02T04:41:50Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: No bank point defines efficiency as output from fewest inputs and effectiveness as meeting objectives; the closest, Efficiency ratios, covers only expense and receivable ratios, and Financial objectives mentions efficiency only in passing.

draft.title: Efficiency and effectiveness
card: making the most output from the fewest inputs. It is about how well resources are used, such as less waste, time or cost for each unit made.
how well a business meets its objectives. It is about whether the business achieves what it set out to do, such as a sales target or a quality standard.
A business can be efficient but not effective. It might make goods cheaply and quickly, but if the goods do not reach its objective, it is not effective.
A business can also be effective but not efficient. It might meet its objective, but use more inputs than it needs to.
draft.remember: Efficiency is about using inputs well. Effectiveness is about reaching objectives.

a.q: A factory cuts the electricity and labour hours it uses for each kettle it makes. Output stays the same. What has improved?
opts: Both, as they mean the same thing
Neither, as output has not changed
a.why: The same output now needs fewer inputs, so efficiency has improved. Effectiveness is about meeting objectives, and nothing here says an objective was met.
a.clue: Look at what happened to the inputs for each kettle.

b.q: Tomas's Melbourne print shop set an objective of delivering every order on time. It now runs its machines with little waste, but a third of orders arrive late. How is the shop best described?
b.why: Little waste suggests inputs are used well, so it is efficient. Late orders mean it is missing its objective, so it is not effective. Calling it effective would confuse low waste with meeting the on-time objective.
b.clue: Compare the shop's use of inputs with its on-time objective.

problems.detail: "if the goods do not reach its objective" is awkward and unclear, since goods do not reach objectives. A clearer version: "if making them does not meet its objective, such as a quality standard".

check.summary: Both questions are sound and match the card and the VCE definitions. The only issue is one awkward card phrase, "the goods do not reach its objective", which should be reworded.
